maml:description.maml:para: Marks which Tier Zero accounts are held in a PAM tool

Adds an InPAM property to each Tier Zero account, set to True where a PAM account matches it.
A PAM account matches when its user name and address match the SamAccountName and the DNS or NetBIOS domain name of the Tier Zero account. A user name in DOMAIN\user or user@domain form matches on the domain in the user name, whatever the address. A user name in user@domain form also matches the UserPrincipalName of the Tier Zero account. Matching is case insensitive.
PAM accounts can come from any source, such as a CSV export or the psPAS Get-PASAccount command.
Name of the PAM account property holding the domain of the account.
Tier Zero account, as output by Get-TierZeroAccount or read from a CSV file it was exported to.
Accounts held in the PAM tool. An empty list marks every account as not held.
Name of the PAM account property holding the user name of the account.

maml:alert.maml:para:
The input objects are returned with the InPAM property added, replacing any existing InPAM property.
The defaults for -UserNameProperty and -AddressProperty match the account objects returned by psPAS.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` PS C:\> $PAMAccounts = Get-PASAccount PS C:\> Get-TierZeroAccount | Compare-TierZeroAccount -PAMAccount $PAMAccounts | Where-Object { -not $_.InPAM } ```
Lists the Tier Zero accounts not held in CyberArk, using psPAS

``` PS C:\> $PAMAccounts = Import-Csv -Path .\PAMExport.csv PS C:\> Get-TierZeroAccount | Compare-TierZeroAccount -PAMAccount $PAMAccounts -UserNameProperty Account -AddressProperty Domain | Export-Csv -Path .\Coverage.csv -NoTypeInformation ```
Writes the PAM coverage of each Tier Zero account to a CSV file, matching against an export with Account and Domain columns
``` PS C:\> Import-Csv -Path .\TierZero.csv | Compare-TierZeroAccount -PAMAccount $PAMAccounts ```
Checks a previously saved Tier Zero account list

maml:description.maml:para: Formats Tier Zero accounts for onboarding to a PAM tool

Outputs an onboarding record for each Tier Zero user account, with userName, address, platformID and SafeName properties.
The output can be exported to CSV for bulk onboarding, or piped to the psPAS Add-PASAccount command.
Accounts which are not user objects, such as computers, managed service accounts and foreign security principals, are skipped.
DNS domain name of the account, used as the address.
Directory object class of the account. Only user accounts are output.
ID of the PAM platform to assign to the accounts.
Name of the safe to onboard the accounts to.
Logon name of the account, used as the user name.

maml:alert.maml:para:
No password is set; the PAM tool must reconcile or change the password after onboarding.
The built-in krbtgt accounts are user accounts and are output; exclude them where the PAM tool should not manage them.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` PS C:\> Get-TierZeroAccount | ConvertTo-PAMAccount -SafeName T0-Accounts -PlatformID WinDomain | Export-Csv -Path .\Onboard.csv -NoTypeInformation ```
Writes an onboarding file for every Tier Zero user account

``` PS C:\> Get-TierZeroAccount | Compare-TierZeroAccount -PAMAccount (Get-PASAccount) | Where-Object { -not $_.InPAM -and $_.Enabled } | ConvertTo-PAMAccount -SafeName T0-Accounts -PlatformID WinDomain | Add-PASAccount ```
Onboards every enabled Tier Zero user account not already held in CyberArk, using psPAS

maml:description.maml:para: Outputs one row per Tier Zero account or group per reason

Flattens Tier Zero accounts or groups into one row for each reason the account or group was found, for CSV export or review in a spreadsheet.
Each row holds the properties of the account, with multi-valued properties joined by '; ', followed by the Source, TierZeroGroup, Path, Right, ObjectType and Target of the reason. Path is the chain of groups joined by ' > '.
Properties added to the account by other commands, such as InPAM from Compare-TierZeroAccount, are kept.
A Tier Zero account or group, as output by Get-TierZeroAccount or Get-TierZeroGroup.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` PS C:\> Get-TierZeroAccount | ConvertTo-TierZeroReport | Export-Csv -Path .\TierZero.csv -NoTypeInformation ```
Writes every Tier Zero account, and every reason each was found, to a CSV file
``` PS C:\> Get-TierZeroAccount | Compare-TierZeroAccount -PAMAccount (Get-PASAccount) | ConvertTo-TierZeroReport | Export-Csv -Path .\Coverage.csv -NoTypeInformation ```
Writes the Tier Zero accounts, their reasons and whether each is held in CyberArk to a CSV file

maml:description.maml:para: Lists the Tier Zero accounts of an Active Directory domain

Lists every account with Tier Zero access to a domain, with the reasons it was found.
Accounts are found three ways:
- GroupMembership: direct, nested and primary group members of the default Tier Zero groups and of any additional groups. The default groups are those rated Tier Zero by the SpecterOps Tier Zero Table (https://specterops.github.io/TierZeroTable/) which can be identified by SID: Administrators, Account Operators, Server Operators, Print Operators, Backup Operators, Incoming Forest Trust Builders, Performance Log Users, Distributed COM Users, Cryptographic Operators, Domain Admins, Domain Controllers, Cert Publishers, Key Admins, plus the forest root groups Enterprise Admins, Schema Admins and Enterprise Key Admins. - WellKnownAccount: the built-in Administrator account, the krbtgt accounts, and read-only domain controller computer accounts. - ContainerACL: principals granted control (GenericAll, GenericWrite, WriteDacl, WriteOwner, or a write or extended right which allows takeover) of the domain root, CN=Users, AdminSDHolder, the Domain Controllers OU, and every container holding a Tier Zero account or group. - ObjectACL: principals granted the same control of a Tier Zero account or group object itself, by an entry set on the object or by owning it, and the managedBy principal of a read-only domain controller. Owners are treated as having full control, as an owner can always change the permissions. Groups found by ContainerACL or ObjectACL are expanded, and the accounts and groups found are checked in turn until no new principal is found.
Each account is listed once, with a Reason property holding a Deetz.TierZeroReason object for every way it was found:
- Source: GroupMembership, WellKnownAccount, ContainerACL or ObjectACL. - TierZeroGroup: the Tier Zero group, or the group granted a right, through which the account was found. - Path: the chain of groups from TierZeroGroup down to the group holding the account. - Right and ObjectType: the right held, such as GenericAll (All), WriteProperty (member), Owner (All) or managedBy. - Target: the container or object the right is held over.
The Source and TierZeroGroup properties of the account list the distinct values of its reasons. The table view summarises the reasons by source, such as GroupMembership (2), ObjectACL (1). Use ConvertTo-TierZeroReport to output one row per account per reason, for CSV export. Groups are not listed; their members are. Use Get-TierZeroGroup to list the Tier Zero groups.
Names of further groups whose members are Tier Zero, such as DnsAdmins or groups which administer Tier Zero systems. Accepts any identity Get-ADGroup accepts in the target domain.
Credential used for all directory queries. Defaults to the current user.
DNS name of the domain to check. Defaults to the domain of the current computer.
Find accounts by group membership and well known account only, without reading container or object security descriptors.

maml:alert.maml:para:
Requires the ActiveDirectory module and read access to the domains of the forest.
Forest level groups are read from the forest root domain. A forest domain which cannot be queried is reported with a warning, and principals from it are not resolved.
Everyone, Anonymous Logon, Authenticated Users, Domain Users, Domain Computers, Users, Guests and Pre-Windows 2000 Compatible Access are not expanded when found in an ACL; a warning is written instead, since every account would be Tier Zero.
Only entries set directly on a Tier Zero account or group object are reported as ObjectACL; inherited entries are found through the container they are set on. The ACLs of Group Policy objects are not analysed. Access control entries scoped to a specific child object type are treated as applying to all objects.
Foreign security principals are listed, translated to DOMAIN\name where the SID resolves. Foreign security principals for groups in a trusted domain are expanded in that domain where it can be read.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` PS C:\> Get-TierZeroAccount ```
Lists the Tier Zero accounts of the current domain
``` PS C:\> Get-TierZeroAccount -Domain child.corp.local -Credential (Get-Credential) | ConvertTo-TierZeroReport | Export-Csv -Path .\TierZero.csv -NoTypeInformation ```
Writes the Tier Zero accounts of the child.corp.local domain, and every reason each was found, to a CSV file
``` PS C:\> Get-TierZeroAccount -AdditionalGroup DnsAdmins, 'Exchange Trusted Subsystem' ```
Lists the Tier Zero accounts of the current domain, treating members of DnsAdmins and Exchange Trusted Subsystem as Tier Zero
``` PS C:\> Get-TierZeroAccount -SkipAclAnalysis -Verbose ```
Lists the Tier Zero accounts found by group membership only, reporting each group as it is checked
``` PS C:\> (Get-TierZeroAccount | Where-Object SamAccountName -eq 'alice').Reason ```
Lists every reason the alice account was found

maml:description.maml:para: Lists the Tier Zero groups of an Active Directory domain

Lists every group with Tier Zero access to a domain, with the reasons it was found.
Discovery is the same as Get-TierZeroAccount; this command outputs the groups found instead of their member accounts.
Groups are found five ways:
- DefaultGroup: the groups rated Tier Zero by the SpecterOps Tier Zero Table (https://specterops.github.io/TierZeroTable/) which can be identified by SID, in the domain and forest root. - AdditionalGroup: groups named by the AdditionalGroup parameter. - GroupMembership: groups nested, directly or through other groups, in a Tier Zero group, including groups in a trusted domain added through a foreign security principal. - ContainerACL: groups granted control of the domain root, CN=Users, AdminSDHolder, the Domain Controllers OU, or a container holding a Tier Zero account or group. - ObjectACL: groups granted control, or ownership, of a Tier Zero account or group object, and groups managing a read-only domain controller.
Default groups are not given ContainerACL or ObjectACL reasons, as they hold rights over most containers by default.
Each group is listed once, with a Reason property holding a Deetz.TierZeroReason object for every way it was found. For GroupMembership reasons, Path is the chain of groups from TierZeroGroup down to the group holding this group. For ContainerACL and ObjectACL reasons, Right, ObjectType and Target describe the right held; reasons from a group nested in a group holding the right also carry its TierZeroGroup and Path.
MemberCount is the number of direct members in the member attribute; it excludes members holding the group as their primary group. Use ConvertTo-TierZeroReport to output one row per group per reason, for CSV export.
Names of further groups to treat as Tier Zero, such as DnsAdmins or groups which administer Tier Zero systems. Accepts any identity Get-ADGroup accepts in the target domain.
Credential used for all directory queries. Defaults to the current user.
DNS name of the domain to check. Defaults to the domain of the current computer.
Find groups by default, additional and nested group only, without reading container or object security descriptors.

maml:alert.maml:para:
Requires the ActiveDirectory module and read access to the domains of the forest.
The notes of Get-TierZeroAccount on broad principals, inherited entries, Group Policy objects and trusted domains apply.

maml:introduction.maml:para: ``` PS C:\> Get-TierZeroGroup ```
Lists the Tier Zero groups of the current domain
Lists the groups which are Tier Zero through nesting or rights, rather than by default
Lists Tier Zero groups whose adminCount is not set, as they are not protected by AdminSDHolder
``` PS C:\> Get-TierZeroGroup -Domain child.corp.local | ConvertTo-TierZeroReport | Export-Csv -Path .\TierZeroGroups.csv -NoTypeInformation ```
Writes the Tier Zero groups of the child.corp.local domain, and every reason each was found, to a CSV file
